content: 1. The use of tranexamic acid for the treatment of postpartum hemorrhage is associated with a reduction of 0 fewer cases per 1,000 patients, with a confidence interval ranging from 16 fewer to 16 more cases. This recommendation is supported by moderate-certainty evidence and is considered critical by the World Health Organization (WHO). 2. When assessing the effect of tranexamic acid on postpartum hemorrhage, the data indicate 0 fewer cases per 1,000 patients, with a confidence interval ranging from 1 fewer to 1 more case. This finding is based on moderate-certainty evidence and is deemed critical in importance. 3. The WHO recommendation on tranexamic acid for postpartum hemorrhage treatment includes an assessment of baby outcomes. While no specific baby outcomes are reported, complications related to the procedure could potentially arise. The confidence interval for this analysis crosses the line of no effect, indicating uncertainty in the results. 4. A single study with design limitations, such as the absence of blinding, reported few events, a small sample size, and a wide confidence interval crossing the line of no effect. This limits the reliability of the findings. 5. Moderate statistical heterogeneity was observed, which may also reflect clinical heterogeneity. Additionally, some analyses were based on single studies with small sample sizes, further limiting the robustness of the evidence. 6. The WHO recommendation on tranexamic acid for postpartum hemorrhage treatment is supported by data from the WOMAN trial, a large multicenter randomized controlled trial involving 20,060 women. This trial provides critical evidence for the use of tranexamic acid in this context. 7. The effect of tranexamic acid on postpartum hemorrhage outcomes shows an increase of 2 more cases per 1,000 patients, with a confidence interval ranging from 6 fewer to 13 more cases. This finding is based on moderate-certainty evidence and is considered critical in importance. 8. Another analysis indicates 1 more case per 1,000 patients, with a confidence interval ranging from 11 fewer to 16 more cases. This is also supported by moderate-certainty evidence and is deemed critical. 9. In a separate assessment, the use of tranexamic acid resulted in 2 fewer cases per 1,000 patients, with a confidence interval ranging from 6 more to 8 fewer cases. This finding is based on moderate-certainty evidence and is considered critical. 10. Wide 95% confidence intervals crossing the line of no effect were observed in several analyses, indicating uncertainty in the effect estimates.
